summary: The main article describes a triethylborane-initiated radical addition to tricyclo[1.1.1.0 1,3]pentane (TCP) to synthesize functionalized bicyclo[1.1.1]pentanes (BCPs). It includes one optimization table, two schemes for derivatization and complex molecule synthesis, and three figures covering bioisostere concepts, substrate scope, and theoretical reaction pathways.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: (a) Bicyclo[1.1.1.0 1,3]pentanes (BCPs) as 1,4-disubstituted arene bioisosteres. (b) BCP as a tert-butyl bioisostere. (c) Approaches to 1-halo-3-substituted BCPs in previous and current work.
items.description: Illustrates the concept of BCPs as bioisosteres for arenes and tert-butyl groups, and compares the current radical approach to previous synthetic methods.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of triethylborane-promoted tricyclopentane ring-opening
items.description: Presents the screening of reaction conditions including initiator loading, temperature, and equivalents of TCP for the ring-opening reaction.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Synthesis of 1-iodo- and 1-bromo-3-substituted BCPs.
items.description: Displays the substrate scope of the triethylborane-initiated ATRA reaction with various alkyl iodides and bromides.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: (a) BCP deiodination. (b) BCP iodide functionalization.
items.description: Shows the reduction of BCP iodides using TTMSS and further transformations into alcohols, aldehydes, and heterocycles.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Synthesis of nucleoside, dipeptide, and pharmaceutical BCP analogues.
items.description: Demonstrates the application of the methodology to the synthesis of BCP-containing nucleosides, peptides, and a fentanyl analogue.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Theoretical analysis of the reaction pathway.
items.description: Provides a computational energy profile for the radical addition and halogen atom transfer steps to explain the selectivity over oligomerization.
